 By Steve Millar | smillar@chicagotribune.com | Daily Southtown PUBLISHED: October 29, 2026 at 5:00 AM CDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Mount Carmel, St. Rita, Oak Lawn, Morgan Park and Providence are the picks to click for the first round of the IHSA playoffs.
 Marist (6-4) at Mount Carmel (7-2)
 Kickoff: 6:30 p.m. Friday.
 Matchup breakdown: A pair of Catholic League Blue rivals get together again in this Class 8A game.
 It’s a rematch from Week 4, when the Caravan scored 28 points in the fourth quarter to pull away for a 56-26 win after the RedHawks had gotten within eight in the fourth.
 That was a breakout game for junior tight end Ty Kennedy, who had two TD catches and has continued to shine for Mount Carmel, which now begins its quest for a fifth straight state championship.
 Marist hopes to establish more on the ground this time around after senior running back Conor Hunt piled up 142 yards and three TDs in a 49-28 opening-round win over Neuqua Valley.
 X-factor: Nathan Samuels , Mount Carmel, senior, running back.
 Steve Millar’s prediction: Mount Carmel.
 Buffalo Grove (7-3) at St. Rita (6-3)
 Kickoff: 7 p.m. Friday.
 Matchup breakdown: St. Rita takes plenty of momentum into its first playoff test in Class 7A.
 The Mustangs have won four straight games and earned the Catholic League Green title with a big 17-14 victory in Week 9 over Nazareth.
 Senior quarterback John Fennell was named the league’s offensive player of the year, while senior Mitch Street earned lineman of the year honors.
 Buffalo Grove escaped an upset bid from Andrew in the opening round, stopping a late 2-point conversion attempt to hold on for a 28-27 win.
 Senior running back/linebacker Matthew Kaput is a two-way force for the Bison.
 X-factor: Kyle Keyser , St. Rita, senior, running back/defensive back/kick returner.
 Steve Millar’s prediction: St. Rita.
 Oak Lawn's Jayden Schlosser (44) tries to get past Evergreen Park's Garret Kazmierowicz (40) during a South Suburban Red game in Evergreen Park on Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. (Vincent D. Johnson / Daily Southtown) 
 Simeon (5-5) at Oak Lawn (7-2)
 Kickoff: 7:30 p.m. Friday.
 Matchup breakdown: This Class 6A game represents a huge opportunity for Oak Lawn.
 The Spartans, who qualified for the playoffs for the first time in 16 years last season but lost to St. Laurence in the first round, have not won a postseason game since 1991.
 That could change thanks to Oak Lawn’s dynamic running attack, led by senior running back Jayden Schlosser , the South Suburban Red’s player of the year.
 Senior lineman Justin Lopez is among the defensive leaders for the Spartans.
 Simeon beat Lindblom 36-11 in the opening round and has some top-level talent. Senior running back James Bell and sophomore receiver Jalonny Billingsley both have high-major offers.
 X-factor: Kamari Polk , Oak Lawn, junior, running back.
 Steve Millar’s prediction: Oak Lawn.
 Morgan Park's Ronald Smith Jr. (1) drops back on a 2-point conversion pass against Kenwood during the Public League city championship game in Chicago on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. (Vincent D. Johnson / for the Chicago Tribune) 
 Oak Forest (6-4) vs. Morgan Park (8-1)
 Kickoff: Noon Saturday at Stagg Stadium.
 Matchup breakdown: In Class 5A, Morgan Park begins its quest to become the first Public League team to win a state championship since Phillips took the 5A title in 2017.
 The Mustangs have gotten exceptional play all season from junior quarterback Ronald Smith Jr. Senior defensive back Darrell Mattison , an Ole Miss recruit, is a major playmaker whenever someone dares to throw the ball in his direction.
 Oak Forest rolled to a 56-6 win over Danville in the opening round, and the Bengals hope to be getting hot at the right time again after making it all the way to the semifinals last fall.
 Senior running back/defensive back Neiko LeFlore was named the South Suburban Blue’s player of the year, while senior running back William McMaster is also dependable on the ground for the Bengals.
 X-factor: Ulysses Morales , Oak Forest, senior, kicker/punter.
 Steve Millar’s prediction: Morgan Park.
 Providence’s Dominic Vita (2) hands the ball off to Broden Mackert (24) against Nazareth during a Catholic League crossover game in La Grange Park on Friday, Sept. 18, 2026. (James C. Svehla / Daily Southtown) 
 Providence (7-3) at Kankakee (7-2)
 Kickoff: 1 p.m. Saturday.
 Matchup breakdown: In the final Illinois Media rankings for Class 5A, voted on at the end of the regular season, Kankakee was No. 2 and Providence sat at No. 4, but the two title contenders meet in the first round.
 Providence had no trouble with Mount Vernon in its 49-13 opening-round win as junior quarterback Dominic Vita threw a pair of TD passes. Meanwhile, senior running back Broden Mackert , the Catholic League Orange’s offensive player of the year, looked healthy and ready to go after missing time with an injury.
 Kankakee, which forfeited a Week 5 game to Lincoln-Way West for using an ineligible player, has only lost on the field once this season, falling 22-14 to Lincoln-Way East in Week 2.
 Senior quarterback Phillip Turner has thrown for 1,092 yards and 17 TDs and ran for 599 yards and five more scores for the Kays.
 X-factor: Brayden McKay , Providence, junior, running back/linebacker/kick returner.
 Steve Millar’s prediction: Providence.
